gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-julius-sans-one: Bold and glowing, Tilt Neon pushes tube-like letters forward with a splayed c. Julius Sans One is the quiet counterweight, its sparse, widely spaced sans letters leaving generous blank room around every curve.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-montserrat-alternate: Montserrat Alternates brings open, chalk-like lowercase that crowds toward the capital line, round and contemporary. And Unica One, the heading, counters with a huge lowercase eye and strokes drawn at a single thickness.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-lexend-exa: Wallpoet towers with high-rising lowercase and a stencil-like gap where the paper shows through between its letters. Lexend Exa takes the opposite route: sturdy, wide-open sans-serif curves with no stroke variation, stubby ascenders and a big x-height.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-lexend-tera: Loud, stretched and spacious, Warnes lets its ink strokes taper off before they ever touch, with zero contrast. Lexend Tera follows with sans letters standing far apart like stepping stones.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-lexend-peta: A mean line set high and ink that looks poured at one width give Luckiest Guy its loud, cheerful bluster. Lexend Peta backs it up with plain sans curves; try it at a modest size.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-lexend-zetta: Nostalgic and bookish, Mystery Quest opens the jaws of every curve above compact ascenders and tall lowercase. Lexend Zetta then carries paragraphs in widely tracked plain sans, tall-bodied letters cut like ribbon, which keeps a long read approachable.
gen-irish-grover-gf-julius-sans-one: Fun and wobbly-warm, with sturdy words. Irish Grover is best at big tall lowercase and joins that thin gently, while Julius Sans One is best at hushed plain sans letters with wide gaps between them.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend-exa: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters, each stroke ending at the same measured thickness beneath a skyward x-height line. Lexend Exa matches that uniform line with wide, distinct curves in plain sans.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend-mega: Bowls that fill the whole line, like bent steel rod. Lexend Mega keeps a longer stretch of text friendly, since its one-nib sans strokes and gapped c shapes stay easy to follow.
gen-tourney-gf-lexend-peta: Tourney stretches its bulky, oversized small letters with wide tracking, every stroke cut to a single width. Lexend Peta, a friendly sans-serif, suits a smaller size beneath it.
